problem: Self-supervised representation learning relies on curated static datasets, while embodied agents must gather their own data; RL-only vision encoders get noisy sparse supervision and separate exploration heuristics (counts, random) do not yield data that is visually informative for the representation learner.
motivation: Biological agents explore actively to acquire visual experience, and a good task-agnostic visual encoder learned without labels would help downstream navigation with little RL data. The observation is that a representation model's own loss is a natural novelty signal: it is high only on unfamiliar images, so an exploration policy rewarded by it should gather diverse, hard data.
key_idea: Jointly train an RL exploration policy to maximize the loss of a self-supervised (SimCLR contrastive) representation model while that model minimizes the loss on the images the policy collects, forming a minimax curiosity game.
insight: Making the exploration reward the representation loss gives more diverse data (higher contrastive loss, LPIPS diversity 0.728 vs 0.717 learned counts vs 0.708 random) and better representations than random or count-based exploration under the same contrastive learner. Freezing the pretrained encoder downstream is crucial (unfrozen ObjectNav SoftSPL rises much more slowly), and representations do not help PointNav with a compass (frozen vs unfrozen identical), so gains appear only where vision matters. ImageNet features surprisingly do not help RL much, and CRL beats them on ImageNav/ObjectNav RL.
method: Contrastive representation model: ResNet50 (group norm) plus 2-layer MLP projection head (128-d) trained with SimCLR InfoNCE (tau=0.07) using flips, random resized crops and color augmentation on frames in the PPO buffer.

Curiosity reward: RL reward is the representation loss; because the full InfoNCE loss can be maximized by standing still (identical images inflate the denominator), only the numerator is used: r_t = -sim(x1,x2) + 1, normalized by the running std of past rewards.

Policy: ResNet + LSTM (512) actor-critic trained with PPO on the intrinsic reward, updated jointly with the representation model from the same minibatches (10M frames on Habitat Matterport3D, 16 envs, RGB 256x256).

Minimax objective: max over policy, min over representation model of the expected representation loss on policy-sampled images. Any representation objective (colorization, contrastive colorization, RND) can be swapped in.
Downstream transfer: freeze the ResNet50 avgpool features and train only the policy heads for ImageNav (Gibson), ObjectNav (MP3D), VLN Seq2Seq with BC/DAgger, or a linear classifier on Places.

setting.backbone: ResNet50 encoder (self-supervised contrastive, from scratch) + LSTM PPO policy; downstream recurrent RL / Seq2Seq policies with frozen encoder
setting.training_data: Pretrain: 10M interaction frames of self-collected RGB in Habitat Matterport3D with no labels; downstream 10M frames RL per task, VLN-CE (Krantz et al.) imitation data
setting.observation: monocular RGB 256x256 only (no depth, no GPS/compass)
setting.action_space: low-level: move forward 0.25 m, turn left/right 30°, look up/down 10° (pretraining); Habitat forward/left/right for downstream
setting.simulator: Habitat (Matterport3D, Gibson), also ViZDoom and Carla

numbers.backbone: ResNet50 CRL frozen + recurrent RL policy
numbers.extra: RGB only, 10M frames, mean over 5 seeds

numbers.backbone: ResNet50 CRL frozen + recurrent RL policy

numbers_note: Benchmarks are Habitat ImageNav (Gibson) and ObjectNav (MP3D) trained with only 10M RGB frames, so values are very low and not comparable with standard leaderboards. Table 1 caption says both 5 and 3 seeds.
results: CRL-pretrained frozen features give the best SPL/SoftSPL on RGB-only ImageNav (0.0324/0.219) and ObjectNav (0.0144/0.119), beating random and learned-counts exploration, ATC, RND, PointNav-policy and ImageNet init (except PointNav policy's higher ObjectNav SPL of 0.0390 in the table). On VLN it beats RND/ATC/scratch and is comparable to ImageNet (BC better, DAgger slightly worse), and on Places linear probe reaches 21.22 top-1 vs ATC 14.83, but far below ImageNet 54.59.
limitations: Absolute navigation numbers are very low (RGB-only, 10M frames) with high seed variance, and differences over baselines are small and often within error.
Representations are still far below ImageNet on real-image recognition and do not help PointNav; the reward needs a workaround (numerator only) to avoid degenerate standing-still behavior.
Requires freezing the encoder downstream; only simulated pretraining, mostly a single contrastive objective.
